title: Selling the Doorstep
passage:
A milk round was bought and sold like a shop, and advertised in the same columns. The pony, the float and the cans were valued and paid for separately; the round itself was reckoned in weeks of takings. Nothing in the bargain bound a customer. Any house could turn the float away at the gate and take the same milk next morning, at the price the dairy fixed, from whoever came by. One clause covered the first thirteen weeks: a customer who fell off the round inside them was struck out of the reckoning, and the price came down by that customer's weeks of takings. What the houses owed on the day of the change stayed the seller's to collect. Kezia Hobbage bought the Netherstall round in January 1923, paying £168 for a hundred and twenty houses taking £21 a week, and £34 for the plant. Nine houses were gone by April, and £12 12s came back to her. She drove it herself until 1938 and sold it on the same terms.
– Leonard Hollinbray

questions.prompt: What can be concluded here about the sale of a milk round?

options.text: A round was priced by the number of houses on it, and the plant was valued on top of that.
Because the plant was valued on its own, what a buyer paid turned mainly on the debts against the houses.
Once the thirteen weeks were up, the buyer alone carried the loss of a house that left.
Any house could change roundsmen overnight, which kept the price of milk in the town down.

questions.rationale: TYPE-002, one_inch_inference read off the LIMIT of a stated rule. The passage gives the rule and never its complement: 'One clause covered the first thirteen weeks: a customer who fell off the round inside them was struck out of the reckoning, and the price came down by that customer's weeks of takings.' Three further facts hold the inference in place. (i) Nothing tied a house to a round - 'Nothing in the bargain bound a customer', and any house could 'turn the float away at the gate and take the same milk next morning, at the price the dairy fixed, from whoever came by' - so customers could leave at any time, not only early. (ii) What the purchase price bought was the round itself, the plant having been 'valued and paid for separately'. (iii) The one worked case shows the clause operating inside its window: Kezia Hobbage bought in January, nine houses were gone by April, and money came back. Put together these license C: the deduction stops at thirteen weeks, houses stayed free to leave after that, and the text supplies no other remedy - so a house lost in week fourteen, or in 1930, reduced nothing, and its share of the £168 stayed spent. The passage never draws the conclusion and nobody in it comments; the reader has to read the edge of the clause rather than the clause. The arithmetic corroborates without being needed: £168 is eight weeks of £21; a hundred and twenty houses taking £21 a week average 3s 6d each; nine houses at eight weeks each is exactly the £12 12s repaid - so the refund confirms that those nine fell inside the window, which is the case the key asks the reader to look past. A = too-literal restatement with one detail bent. Its second clause is quoted straight from the passage (the plant was indeed valued on its own), which lends the whole option borrowed credibility, and 'a hundred and twenty houses' is the most salient figure in the text; but the price is fixed by takings, not by headcount - 'reckoned in weeks of takings' - and the deduction likewise falls 'by that customer's weeks of takings', not by a flat per-house sum. A reader still in retrieval mode takes it. B = half-right conjunction, and the set's only hedged option. Its premise is true and quotable, and 'mainly' makes the verdict sound measured rather than sweeping; but the passage forecloses that verdict twice over - the round was 'reckoned in weeks of takings', and 'What the houses owed on the day of the change stayed the seller's to collect', so the standing debts were not in the bargain at all and cannot be what the price turned on. A reader who stops at the comma takes it. D = scope-shift onto the town's milk market, carried by ordinary competition reasoning the passage does not supply. Its first clause is a fair reading of the free-switching sentence, so it feels anchored; but the milk came 'at the price the dairy fixed' whoever brought it, which leaves rival roundsmen nothing to compete on, and the text says nothing whatever about the level of milk prices or about any pressure on them. It answers a different question from the one the stem asks. Hedge balance: the key is a flat, unhedged assertion and the one cautious-sounding option (B, 'turned mainly on') is wrong, so 'pick the qualified answer' scores nothing here. No option carries a hard absolutizer. Measured with mech.py tokenize the key runs 17 tokens against A 20, B 20 and D 16 - third of four, never the longest.
